title: Inspection Ledger
prompt: Create a high-fidelity 1440x900 desktop web application UI composition for Curbcut, a browser-native accessibility repair workbench. This must look like a real professional developer tool screenshot, not a poster or marketing page. Precision-light visual world: cool white and pale gray surfaces, near-black ink, disciplined cobalt blue focus, amber proposed state, emerald verified state, restrained red issue severity; no gradients, no neon, no glass, no excessive rounded cards. Composition option B, Inspection Ledger: a slim top utility bar with Curbcut, revision, secure sandbox, WebMCP connected, Scan, Undo, Import, Export. The main work area uses three panes: a narrower left HTML/CSS editor with line numbers, a wide center live checkout preview on a clean canvas, and a right evidence ledger with vertically stacked issue rows and an expanded selected issue. The right pane feels like a rigorous QA ledger: severity chips, rule ID, exact line/column, mapped target, WCAG tags, remediation classification, before/after diff, and distinct Approve/Reject controls. Source and preview remain simultaneously visible. At the bottom, a compact two-line activity strip shows agent scan, inspect, preview and human approval events with timestamps. Show an amber proposed preview toggle beside Working, and one emerald Verified after rescan result. Crisp typographic hierarchy, flat surfaces, 1px rules, 4-6px corners, system sans plus mono data. No chatbot, no marketing hero, no illustrations.
